page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ine.large is an x86_64 virtualization instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon Sapphire Rapids processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 4.0 GB allocated per virtual core. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are included in this configuration.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps, while zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The instance includes no local storage, requiring attached network-based block storage volumes for persistent data. This architectural separation offloads storage management to external block volumes while keeping the compute node stateless.

With dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.g8ine.large delivers consistent execution without resource contention from neighboring virtual machines. The balanced compute and memory profile fits standard workloads such as lightweight web serving, application backends, containerized microservices, and small database deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ine.large is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It offers 2 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon Sapphire Rapids processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of memory to maintain a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The instance does not feature onboard GPUs and provides no integrated local storage, directing users toward attached network storage solutions. Baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted. With dedicated CPU allocation, this configuration avoids noisy-neighbor performance fluctuations while keeping resource consumption balanced. The ecs.g8ine.large is engineered for standard enterprise workloads, including web servers, application gateways, microservice staging environments, and modest relational database systems.
